segments.text: SK Juris & Co. (SKJC) advises and represents businesses, investors and individuals in domestic and international commercial arbitration. Our services extend from drafting arbitration agreements and assessing disputes to conducting proceedings, pursuing settlements and addressing arbitral awards.
We work with clients in Pakistan and overseas through consultations, document preparation, hearings and coordination with counsel in relevant jurisdictions.
1. Arbitration Agreements and Dispute Resolution Clauses
Drafting and review of arbitration clauses in commercial contracts, investment agreements, joint ventures and construction documents.
Advice on institutional or ad hoc arbitration, the seat, procedural rules, language and number of arbitrators.
Consideration of the laws governing the contract, arbitration agreement and arbitral procedure.
Review of dispute provisions across connected contracts, guarantees and project agreements.
Agreements to refer an existing dispute to arbitration.
Assessment of whether the dispute and requested remedies may lawfully be determined through arbitration.
Review of contractual rights, potential claims, defences, evidence and available remedies.
Advice on notices, negotiation periods, contractual escalation procedures and limitation issues.
Assessment of potential liability, recoverability, costs and enforcement considerations.
Identification and preservation of relevant contracts, correspondence, payment records and project documents.
Preparation of settlement proposals and engagement in negotiations before formal proceedings.
3. Jurisdiction and Formation of the Tribunal
Advice on nominations, appointment mechanisms and applications to the relevant institution, appointing authority or court.
Review of disclosures and potential conflicts affecting arbitrators.
Applications concerning the challenge, removal or replacement of arbitrators where available.
Disputes over the existence, validity, scope or applicability of an arbitration agreement.
Advice on joinder, consolidation and related proceedings where permitted by the applicable agreements, rules and law.
Requests or notices of arbitration, responses, counterclaims and preliminary applications.

Preparation of witness evidence and coordination with technical, financial and valuation experts.

Applications concerning preservation of assets, evidence, property or the subject matter of the dispute.

Applications to competent courts for interim protection or other support for arbitration.
Advice on security for costs, claims or other obligations where the relevant framework permits.
Assessment and conduct of accelerated procedures where available or agreed.

SKJC provides legal advice to companies, founders, investors, directors and shareholders on business structures, corporate governance, commercial agreements, transactions and disputes.
Services are available to clients in Pakistan and overseas through consultations, document review, drafting, negotiations and continuing legal counsel.
Business establishment: Advice on company structures, ownership arrangements and the legal requirements of establishing a business.
Corporate structures: Holding companies, subsidiaries, joint venture companies and special purpose vehicles.
Constitutional documents: Preparation and review of memoranda, articles of association and other governing documents.
Ownership and capital: Founder interests, investor participation, share subscriptions, allotments, transfers and capital changes.
Continuing requirements: Corporate registrations, statutory records, disclosures and changes to company particulars.
Directors and management: Advice on legal duties, corporate authority, delegated powers and management responsibilities.
Board and shareholder decisions: Meetings, elections, resolutions, voting rights and approval procedures.
Conflicts and related parties: Directors’ interests, related-party transactions and dealings within corporate groups.
Shareholder arrangements: Reserved matters, minority protections, deadlock procedures, succession and exit rights.
Governance documentation: Board charters, committee terms, internal policies and decision-making procedures.
Commercial documentation: Drafting, review and negotiation of agreements supporting business operations.
Trading relationships: Supply, procurement, manufacturing, distribution, agency, dealership and franchise agreements.
Services and technology: Consultancy, management, outsourcing, software licensing and confidentiality agreements.
Business assets: Commercial leases, asset transfers and arrangements concerning operational premises and equipment.
Contractual protection: Payment obligations, performance standards, warranties, indemnities, liability, termination and remedies.
Contract management: Amendments, renewals, assignments, novations and negotiated exits.
Transaction structuring: Mergers, acquisitions, amalgamations, business transfers, divestments and reorganisations.
Investment arrangements: Share purchases, asset purchases, subscriptions, joint ventures and strategic collaborations.
Legal due diligence: Review of ownership, corporate records, licences, material contracts, financing, assets, liabilities and disputes.
Transaction agreements: Term sheets, purchase agreements, subscription agreements, joint venture agreements and shareholders’ agreements.
Approvals and completion: Corporate and regulatory approvals, conditions precedent, disclosures, warranties, indemnities and completion documents.
Post-completion matters: Ownership changes, governance arrangements and continuing obligations.
Business financing: Financing agreements, shareholder funding, guarantees, security documents and intercreditor arrangements.
Investment and fundraising: Legal documentation for private investment, capital raising and investor participation.
Regulated entities: Corporate and regulatory advice concerning banking companies, insurance companies, takaful operators and non-banking finance companies.
Ownership and control: Significant shareholdings, changes of control, governance requirements and regulatory approvals.
Financial restructuring: Refinancing, debt restructuring and negotiated arrangements with lenders and creditors.
Group reorganisations: Consolidation, separation and restructuring of business interests.
Ownership transitions: Shareholder exits, management buyouts and family business succession.
Corporate arrangements: Schemes, compromises, amalgamations and demergers.
Financial distress: Rehabilitation, creditor negotiations and restructuring arrangements.
Company closure: Winding up, liquidation, dissolution, striking off and restoration.
Shareholder disputes: Minority protection, oppression and mismanagement, ownership disputes and shareholder agreement claims.
Board disputes: Director appointments, removals, company meetings, resolutions and control of management.
Transaction disputes: Claims arising from acquisitions, joint ventures, investments and commercial contracts.
Court remedies: Injunctions, declarations, recovery proceedings and protection of company assets before competent courts.
Arbitration and mediation: Representation in agreed dispute resolution procedures, settlement negotiations and related proceedings.
Cross-border proceedings: Coordination with locally admitted counsel where foreign-law advice or local representation is required.
Pakistan Corporate Law and Regulatory Matters
For matters governed by Pakistani law, services include:
SECP and company law: Incorporation, statutory compliance, beneficial ownership, corporate changes and regulatory proceedings under the Companies Act, 2017, and Companies Regulations, 2024.

Listed companies and PSX: Listings, fundraising, disclosures, takeovers and governance under the Securities Act, 2015, applicable Pakistan Stock Exchange Regulations, and Listed Companies (Code of Corporate Governance) Regulations, 2019.

Banking companies and SBP: Advice under the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962, Microfinance Institutions Ordinance, 2001, and applicable State Bank requirements, including financing, ownership changes and recovery matters.
Insurance and takaful: Advice under the Insurance Ordinance, 2000, Insurance Rules, 2017, Takaful Rules, 2012, and applicable governance requirements.
Non-banking finance companies: Licensing and compliance under the NBFC Rules, 2003, and Non-Banking Finance Companies and Notified Entities Regulations, 2008.
Competition and merger clearance: Advice and proceedings before the Competition Commission of Pakistan, including the Competition Act, 2010, and Competition (Merger Control) Regulations, 2016.
Trade organisations and DGTO: Licensing, governance, membership, elections and regulatory proceedings under the Trade Organizations Act, 2013, and Trade Organizations Rules, 2013.
Rehabilitation and restructuring: Advice under the Companies Act, 2017, Corporate Rehabilitation Act, 2018, and other applicable restructuring legislation.
Services for International and Remote Clients
Online consultations: Discussions with business owners, directors, investors and management teams in Pakistan and overseas.
Document review and drafting: Electronic exchange, review and preparation of corporate and commercial documents.
Transaction support: Negotiations, document revisions and coordination of signing and completion requirements.
Continuing counsel: Retained legal advice for business decisions, contractual relationships and developing legal issues.
Jurisdictional coordination: Identification of applicable laws and coordination with counsel in other jurisdictions where required.

SKJC advises businesses, inventors, creators and investors on the protection, ownership, commercialisation and enforcement of intellectual property rights. Our work encompasses trademarks, patents, copyright, industrial designs, confidential information and the agreements through which intellectual property is developed, licensed and transferred.

We assist clients in Pakistan and overseas with domestic matters, international protection strategies and cross-border transactions. Where a matter requires foreign legal advice, registration or representation, we coordinate with appropriately qualified counsel and intellectual property professionals in the relevant jurisdiction.

Identifying intellectual property assets, reviewing ownership and assessing gaps in protection.
Selecting appropriate rights, filing priorities and jurisdictions according to the business, product and intended markets.
Reviewing rights held by founders, employees, consultants, contractors and collaborating businesses.
Advising on renewals, maintenance, assignments, licensing and changes to registered particulars.
Assessing proposed business names, product names, logos and other brand identifiers before adoption or filing.
Preparing and pursuing applications, selecting goods and services, and responding to examination objections.
Advising on oppositions, rectification, cancellation and other challenges available under the applicable law.
Handling assignments, licence arrangements, recordals, renewals and brand-use requirements.
Addressing trademark infringement, passing off, confusingly similar branding and unauthorised commercial use.
Assessing inventions, disclosure risks, ownership and potential filing routes.
Preparing and pursuing applications, with technical drafting and specialist input where required.
Responding to objections and advising on amendments, renewals and patent portfolio requirements.
Reviewing patent licences, infringement risks, validity issues and available challenges.
Coordinating direct and priority-based filings in selected overseas jurisdictions.

Assisting with copyright registration where appropriate, evidence of authorship and ownership records.

Defining rights between clients, agencies, developers, employees and independent creators.
Addressing unauthorised copying, publication, distribution, adaptation and online use.

Advising eligible producers, associations and other stakeholders on registration, authorised use and protection.

Preparing non-disclosure agreements for negotiations, investment discussions, employment and commercial collaboration.
Advising on the protection of technical know-how, formulas, processes, source code and other confidential material.
Reviewing access controls, contractual obligations and procedures for handling confidential information.
Assessing contractual remedies and other protection available under the applicable law.

Advising on abusive registrations and complaints or responses under the UDRP and applicable registry procedures.
Addressing impersonation, counterfeit listings and unauthorised use of trademarks or copyrighted content.
Preparing infringement notices, takedown requests and responses under relevant platform rules.

Structuring settlements and handling IP-related contractual disputes through mediation or arbitration where appropriate.
11. International Intellectual Property and Overseas Clients
Advising on national filings and Madrid System applications where eligibility and territorial requirements are met.
Coordinating applications, renewals, objections and enforcement across selected jurisdictions.
Reviewing brand availability, ownership and licensing arrangements before entering a new market.
